Broncos

Upton Creates History with Third Dally M Medal

Author
broncos.com.au
Timestamp
Thu 1 Oct 2026, 06:21 AM

Share on social media

  • Share via Facebook
  • Share via Twitter
  • Share via Whats-app
  • Share via Reddit
  • Share via Email
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:37
Instaread

Broncos Captain Tamika Upton has made NRLW history, becoming the first player to win consecutive Dally M Medals after taking home the prestigious award at Wednesday night’s ceremony in Sydney.

Upton previously claimed the medal for her standout 2025 season and again while playing for the Newcastle Knights in 2023, making the 29-year-old the first NRLW player to win three Dally M Medals.

The fullback has again been a dominant force for the Broncos in 2026, with 15 tries, 20 try assists and 62 tackle breaks and 20 line breaks with an average of 157 run metres per game. 

Upton has won three premierships with the Broncos in 2019, 2020 and 2025, and will be aiming to add another title to her impressive record when Brisbane play the Sydney Roosters in Sunday’s Grand Final.

“It feels pretty crazy accepting this individual award in a team sport, so I couldn't do this without my teammates," Upton said.

“Got some incredible ones sitting in the room tonight, but a lot of which will be back home watching.

I'm surrounded by some of the best people and like I said before, they always push you to be your best on the field, but off the field as well, and that's what makes our Club so special.

Tamika Upton Broncos Captain

“I have to thank my family as well, they're always supporting me, making the trek.

“I know they'll be all watching from back home, far and wide, all across central Queensland."

The Broncos Captain was one of several Brisbane players recognised at the Dally M Awards, with Jesse Southwell and Julia Robinson also rewarded for outstanding 2026 campaigns.

Robinson was recognised for another consistent season, earning selection at wing in the NRLW Team of the Year.

It is the fourth consecutive year Robinson has been named in the Team of the Year, with the versatile outside back continuing to excel across both wing and centre.

Robinson has scored eight tries, along with 41 tackle breaks, 10 line breaks and two try assists in 2026.

Combining with Upton in the Broncos’ spine, Jesse Southwell was named equal top points scorer for the season.

She has played a key role in Brisbane’s attack, with 55 conversions, 11 try assists, one try and 18 line break assists, while averaging 238 kick metres per game.

Back-rower Lauren Dam and centre Georgia Bartlett were also nominated for Team of the Year and Rookie of the Year respectively. 

The rest of the Broncos' NRLW squad travels to Sydney on Thursday, ahead of Sunday's Grand Final against the Roosters at Accor Stadium.
